chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Al-Nawfali, from Al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'No one chokes when drinking milk,'
because Allah, Mighty and Majestic, says: 'Milk, pure and palatable for the drinkers.'

key_terms.يَغَصُّ: chokes or is obstructed in the throat

ai.seo_question: Why does milk not cause choking according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that 'ghass' refers to the sensation of choking or difficulty in swallowing, attributing milk's smooth texture to its divine creation as 'pure and pleasant.' This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on the natural fit (fitrah) of milk for human consumption, linking physical comfort to Quranic descriptors of divine bounty. The hadith serves as a theological affirmation of milk's suitability, reinforcing the idea that God’s provisions are inherently designed for human ease and health.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Al Nowfaly, from Al Sakuny, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘There is no one who chokes by drinking the milk
because Allahazwj Mighty and Majestic is Saying [16:66] pure milk, palatable for the drinkers’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from al-Nawfaliy from al-Sakuniy who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that the Messenger of Allah, O Allah, grant compensation to Muhammad and his family worthy of their services to Your cause, has said, ‘There is no one who is choked when drinking milk; Allah, most Majestic, most Glorious, says, ‘ . . .pure milk which is suitable for those who drink.’”*
